title: Is a rotated square paper still a square?
description: A square piece of paper is rotated until it looks like a diamond. The video checks its sides and angles after the rotation. Keeko raises the doubt that a square turned on its corner is a different shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: rotating a shape does not change its lengths or its angles, so a rotated square is still a square and a rotated rectangle is still a rectangle. Watch for children who think a diamond is a different shape from a square.

source: A square piece of paper has all its sides equal and all angles 90 degrees. It is rotated. Is it still a square? Are all the sides still equal? Are all the angles still 90 degrees?
video_script.why: The child sees that rotation keeps lengths and angles, so a rotated square keeps both properties of a square.
video_script.substitution: A square piece of paper rotated until it stands like a diamond.
video_script.anchor: A square piece of paper turned until it looks like a diamond
video_script.wrong_answer: a square turned on its corner is a different shape
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a square turned on its corner is a different shape, because it looks like a diamond. Rotation changes only how the paper stands. The sides and the angles are the same ones as before, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the rotated paper is still a square.

final_answer.value: yes, it is still a square; all the sides are still equal and all the angles are still 90 degrees; a rotated rectangle is still a rectangle
final_answer.spoken: yes, the rotated paper is still a square; all the sides are still equal and all the angles are still ninety degrees; a rotated rectangle is still a rectangle

hold_back: rotated paper is still a square
never_show: the verdict on the rotated paper before the answer
maths_rules: A square has S1 all four sides equal and S2 all four angles 90 degrees.
Rotation turns a shape round without bending or stretching it, so every length stays the same.
Rotation keeps every angle the same too, so each angle of the rotated paper is still 90 degrees.
The rotated paper has both properties of a square, so it is a square.
By the same reasoning, a rotated rectangle is still a rectangle.
video_script.design: One idea: rotation does not change lengths or angles. Uses the two properties of a square. Wrong idea: a square on its corner is a different shape. The paper stays all video.
